column2: The sample between two carbon beds contains 0.24 mg/L total chlorine. Where should the technician sample next?
column6: Drain from the reverse osmosis unit
column7: The result exceeds the federal trigger for total chlorine after the first removal stage. Sampling downstream of the second stage checks whether it is still removing chlorine adequately.

column2: Why is hardness checked at the outlet of a water softener near day's end?
column3: To test performance after sustained use
column4: To catch brine before regeneration begins
column5: To estimate the feed water's hardness
column6: To measure the reverse osmosis rejection rate
column7: The end-of-day result checks how well the softener performed after a day's demand, when the resin is closest to exhaustion. Feed-water hardness would characterize what entered the softener.

column2: Feed water measures 200 µS/cm and reverse osmosis permeate measures 10 µS/cm. What is the rejection percentage?
column7: Subtract permeate conductivity from feed conductivity, then divide by feed conductivity. Here, 190 ÷ 200 is 95%.

column2: Which pretreatment component normally removes chloramine from the water supply before reverse osmosis?
column6: Water softener resin bed
column7: Activated carbon removes chloramine and free chlorine from feed water. The softener removes hardness minerals, while sediment and cartridge filters trap particles.

column2: Conductivity is in range. What hazard can an independent pH check still detect in the dialysate?
column6: Microbial growth in the fluid
column7: Conductivity and pH measure different properties. A mixing error can leave the conductivity in range even when the solution is too acidic.

column2: A freshly mixed acid concentrate batch has a label, but its required verification test is pending. Where should it stay?
column6: In the concentrate jugs at stations
column7: Keep the batch out of the distribution system until its test results meet the release criteria. A correct label identifies the formula but does not verify the concentration.

column2: On a 2008T, 36.5 °C is entered and confirmed. The Temp display reads 36.0 °C. What is that reading?
column6: Lower temperature alarm limit
column7: After confirmation, this control shows the machine's measured dialysate temperature. The operator's entered setpoint is the target temperature.

column2: A 2008T repeatedly displays "Flow Error" before treatment. Which condition does the manufacturer direct staff to check first?
column3: Inadequate water supply to the machine
column4: Kinks in the dialyzer supply and return lines
column6: Incorrect drain flow at the prescribed setting
column7: The 2008T guide starts with water supply flow for a recurring Flow Error. Its instructions then check that dialysate flow is on and inspect the dialyzer lines for kinks.

column2: Three glucose meters read high with the same QC material. All pass with a new container of the same level. What should be investigated first?
column3: Storage of the original control vial
column4: The strip lot used on one meter
column5: The service history of one meter
column6: The glucose range printed for another level
column7: The high QC results followed the control vial across all three meters. A fresh vial at the same level produced acceptable readings, so check the original vial's storage, handling and expiry.

column2: In an intact hollow-fiber dialyzer, where does the blood travel as wastes pass into dialysate?
column4: Around the outside of the fibers
column6: Across the pores into the dialysate
column7: Blood travels inside the fibers and dialysate runs outside them. Wastes cross the fiber walls from blood into dialysate while the bulk streams remain separate.

column2: The courier is delayed. Where should a serum tube wait if the laboratory specifies storage at 2 to 8 °C?
column6: Insulated bag with no cold source
column7: A refrigerator maintained in the required range keeps this specimen within the laboratory's transport conditions while it waits. Freezing it would expose it to temperatures below the range given for this test.

column2: A chlorine sample sat for an hour before testing. How should the technician verify the result?
column3: Draw fresh water and test it on site
column4: Repeat the assay on the original sample
column5: Refrigerate the original sample before testing
column6: Send a portion to the outside laboratory
column7: Chloramine can decrease after collection, so a delayed assay can give a falsely low reading. Collect and test a fresh sample promptly following the facility's procedure.

column2: Reverse osmosis flow and pressure remain stable, but permeate conductivity rises. What does that reading suggest?
column3: More dissolved ions in the product
column4: Less water moving to the drain
column5: Lower operating pressure at the pump
column6: More particles clogging the prefilter
column7: Conductivity rises as the level of dissolved ions rises. Normal water flow and pressure describe operating conditions but do not verify that the product water meets quality limits.

column2: Backup deionization alarms for low resistivity. Where should its automatic diversion valve direct the out-of-spec water?
column3: To a drain outside the product loop
column6: To the water distribution loop
column7: A low-resistivity alarm indicates poor ionic water quality. An automatic divert-to-drain valve protects patients by keeping that water out of the distribution system.

column2: What is the name for water that passes through the membrane in a reverse osmosis unit?
column6: Concentrate
column7: Permeate is the product stream that crosses the membrane. Concentrate is the reject stream that carries retained material along the membrane surface.

column2: The available 45X acid matches the prescription, but the machine is labeled 35X. Which replacement should be selected?
column5: Prescribed formula at 45X from another lot
column6: Different formula at 45X with the same potassium
column7: The acid concentrate must match both the prescribed formula and the machine's configured proportioning ratio. A new lot at 45X would still mismatch the machine.

column2: A mixing procedure uses a hydrometer to verify a batch of concentrate. What does it measure?
column6: Total alkalinity
column7: A hydrometer measures specific gravity, which the technician compares with the approved range for the mixture. A pH reading alone could miss a substantial error in the concentrate strength.

column2: After an authorized conversion to a different proportioning ratio, what should the facility monitor in the finished dialysate?
column6: Water hardness at the softener outlet
column7: A machine that has been converted to a different ratio needs verification that it produces dialysate with the expected electrolyte concentrations. Water hardness measurements only characterize the softener's output.

column2: A machine moves between stations. Which fields link repeat service calls for the same alarm?
column6: Station number and service date
column7: A permanent equipment identifier follows the individual machine when it moves. The alarm code distinguishes one reported fault from another on that unit.

column2: An external conductivity meter reads high in its reference solution. What check should be repeated before it verifies dialysate?
column3: Handheld reading against fresh calibration standard
column4: Machine reading against an independent dialysate sample
column5: Reverse osmosis reading against product-water conductivity
column6: pH reading against a fresh buffer standard
column7: A fresh conductivity standard lets the technician check the external meter against a known value. The reading needs to meet the device's tolerance before the meter is used.

column2: Two dialyzers remove fluid at the same rate. Why does one need a smaller pressure difference across its membrane?
column6: Lower sodium sieving coefficient
column7: At a fixed removal rate, a higher dialyzer ultrafiltration coefficient means less pressure is required to move the same volume of water per hour. This coefficient describes the dialyzer as a whole.

column2: The lab rejects clotted specimens for its whole-blood count. What should happen when this tube contains a clot?
column4: Centrifuge and send the cell-free fraction
column5: Resuspend the clot by inverting the tube
column6: Transfer the liquid into a fresh tube
column7: A clot makes a whole-blood specimen unsuitable under the laboratory's stated criteria. Moving the residual liquid to another tube would leave cells trapped in the clot.

column2: Which ion replaces calcium and magnesium during the service cycle of a conventional brine-regenerated water softener?
column6: Chloride
column7: The charged resin exchanges sodium ions for dissolved calcium and magnesium. The brine restores sodium to the resin during regeneration.

column2: Flow through a carbon bed rises while its volume stays fixed. What happens to empty bed contact time?
column3: Shorter because water moves through faster
column4: Longer because the bed processes more water
column5: Unchanged because the bed volume stays fixed
column6: Unchanged unless the inlet pressure also rises
column7: Empty bed contact time is bed volume divided by flow rate. More water moving through the same volume per minute means less contact time.

column2: Both carbon beds let through excessive total chlorine. After repairs, which reading verifies the correction?
column3: Total chlorine in range at the final carbon outlet
column4: Total chlorine in range in the inlet feed
column5: Pressure drop in range across both carbon beds
column6: Reverse osmosis rejection back in range
column7: The facility must verify the result by retesting the treated water for chlorine at the outlet of the final chlorine removal stage. The carbon pressure drop and reverse osmosis rejection measure other system functions.

column2: An RO membrane is replaced between annual tests. Which product-water analysis is due because of the replacement?
column6: Total chlorine residual test
column7: A chemical analysis of product water is due after membrane replacement, even if the annual analysis was recent. Microbiological surveillance checks a different aspect of water quality.

column2: The bicarbonate mixer runs past its validated time. What change can excessive agitation cause in the batch?
column6: Higher free calcium in the finished dialysate
column7: Over-agitation can drive off carbon dioxide and raise the concentrate's pH. Use the prescribed mixing time rather than extending it after the powder has dissolved.

column2: An acid mixing tank still holds concentrate from a different formula. How should it be prepared for the next batch?
column3: Drain the tank completely, then rinse it
column4: Drain to the pump inlet and rinse
column5: Drain the tank completely and refill it
column6: Rinse while adding the new concentrate
column7: Completely draining and rinsing the tank according to the manufacturer's directions prevents carryover from the previous formula. Diluting the remainder leaves some of the old formulation in the next batch.

column2: A 2008T stays in bypass when the dialysate is too cool. Where is the solution routed?
column3: Around the dialyzer inside the machine
column4: Through the blood side of the dialyzer
column5: Back into the incoming treated-water line
column6: Through the dialyzer at a reduced flow
column7: In bypass mode the machine routes dialysate around the dialyzer. A temperature outside the alarm limits can trigger bypass even when dialysate conductivity is acceptable.

column2: A glucose meter passes its electronic self-check but fails with liquid controls. What does the liquid check assess?
column3: How the meter and strips perform together
column4: Whether a patient sample was collected correctly
column5: Agreement with a laboratory glucose method
column6: Whether the meter's internal electronics start up
column7: The liquid control is a sample with a known expected range. It checks the meter and strips together. The electronic test checks internal function without testing a sample on a strip.

column2: A backup machine will run a high-flux dialyzer. What capability must its manufacturer specify for that pairing?
column6: Automatic conductivity compensation
column7: With a high-flux dialyzer, CMS calls for a machine the manufacturer specifies as able to control and monitor fluid removal accurately. The other functions do not establish that capability.

column2: In hollow-fiber hemodialysis, what is the usual direction of dialysate flow relative to blood flow?
column6: Across at right angles
column7: Blood and dialysate travel in opposite directions along the fibers, with the fiber walls separating the streams.

column2: Pre-dialysis BUN is 60 mg/dL and post-dialysis BUN is 15 mg/dL. What is the urea reduction ratio?
column7: BUN fell by 45 mg/dL from a starting value of 60 mg/dL. Dividing the reduction by the starting value gives 75%.

column2: Which continuous measurement indicates how well a deionization unit is removing dissolved ions from dialysis water?
column6: Pressure across the resin bed
column7: Resistivity indicates how strongly the water resists electric current. When ions begin to pass through an exhausted deionizer, resistivity drops.

column2: What does a reverse osmosis unit's recovery percentage describe?
column3: Share of incoming flow made into product
column4: Share of dissolved solutes removed from water
column5: Share of the product diverted to drain
column6: Share of the product meeting chlorine limits
column7: Recovery describes water yield. Rejection describes removal of dissolved substances and is calculated from feed and product conductivity.

column2: A backup deionizer is ready, but the downstream ultrafilter was removed. What protection needs restoring before use?
column3: A barrier against bacteria and endotoxins
column5: Removal of calcium and magnesium ions
column6: Reduction of dissolved salts by ion exchange
column7: Deionization removes dissolved ions but does not substitute for a downstream ultrafilter. The ultrafilter protects the product stream against bacteria and endotoxins.

column2: The facility disinfects its water system after excess bacterial growth. Which follow-up verifies the correction?
column3: Repeat cultures at designated loop sites
column4: Repeat chlorine testing at carbon outlets
column6: Measure hardness at the softener outlet
column7: Repeat cultures check whether the bacterial count fell after disinfection. Testing the carbon outlets or softener would assess separate functions in the water system.

column2: A supplier recalls a shipment of dry acid concentrate. Which mixing log field identifies the affected batches?
column3: Lot numbers of the powder packages
column4: Formula and volume for each batch
column5: Time and date of the latest tank rinse
column6: Name of the technician who mixed it
column7: The lot numbers recorded for the powder packages link the finished batches to the supplier's recall. Several lots can share the same formula, so the recipe alone cannot isolate the recalled material.

column2: A 2008T has finished its rinse after an internal chemical cycle. Which check verifies the rinse worked?
column5: Response of the blood leak detector
column6: Accuracy of the ultrafiltration volume
column7: A completed rinse cycle does not establish that the internal fluid path is clear of disinfectant. Test for residue according to the chemical manufacturer's instructions.

column2: An acid label lists 100 mEq/L sodium from acid and 137 mEq/L in finished dialysate. What explains the difference?
column4: Sodium added during the priming saline rinse
column5: Sodium remaining in purified feed water
column6: Sodium released from the dialyzer membrane
column7: The label distinguishes the sodium that the acid concentrate contributes from the expected total after mixing. Sodium bicarbonate concentrate contributes the additional sodium.

column2: A machine is due for maintenance every 1,000 operating hours. Its last service was at 6,250 hours. Which meter reading first makes it due?
column6: 7,500 hours
column7: Count the next 1,000 operating hours from the service entry at 6,250. The due reading is 7,250 hours, regardless of how long it took to reach it.

column2: Glucose strips expire on the printed date or 90 days after opening, whichever comes first. Which vial can be used?
column3: Opened 70 days ago, printed date next week
column4: Opened 95 days ago, printed date next month
column5: Opened 45 days ago, printed date last week
column6: Opened 100 days ago, printed date yesterday
column7: Both limits must be met. The vial opened 70 days ago is within the 90-day limit, and its printed date has not passed.

column2: What is the name for pressure-driven removal of water across a hemodialyzer membrane?
column6: Adsorption
column7: Ultrafiltration uses a pressure difference across the dialyzer membrane to move water out of the blood. Diffusion moves solutes down a concentration gradient.

column2: Why can red cells breaking open in a collected specimen make its serum potassium result unreliable?
column5: Potassium binds to the tube's separator gel
column6: The serum loses potassium as it cools
column7: Red cells contain substantially more potassium than serum. When they break open in the tube, released potassium can make the measured serum value falsely high.
